text:
A factory produces two types of food, I and II, and currently has 50 skilled workers. It is known that one skilled worker can produce $10 \ \mathrm{kg} / \ \mathrm{h}$ of food I or $6 \ \mathrm{kg} / \ \mathrm{h}$ of food II. According to contract bookings, the weekly demand for these two foods will rise sharply, as shown in Table 1-11. Therefore, the factory has decided to train 50 new workers by the end of the 8th week. It is known that a worker works $40 \ \mathrm{h}$ per week, and a skilled worker can train up to three new workers in two weeks (during the training period, both the skilled worker and the trainees do not participate in production). The weekly wage of a skilled worker is 360 yuan, the weekly wage of a trainee during the training period is 120 yuan, and after training, the wage is 240 yuan per week, with the same production efficiency as skilled workers. During the transition period of training, many skilled workers are willing to work overtime, and the factory has decided to arrange some workers to work $60 \ \mathrm{h}$ per week, with a weekly wage of 540 yuan. If the booked food cannot be delivered on time, the compensation fee for each week of delay per $ \ \mathrm{kg}$ is 0.5 yuan for food I and 0.6 yuan for food II. Under these conditions, how should the factory make comprehensive arrangements to minimize the total cost?

Table 1-11:
| Week | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 |
| I    | 10000 | 10000 | 12000 | 12000 | 16000 | 16000 | 20000 | 20000 |
| II   | 6000 | 7200 | 8400 | 10800 | 10800 | 12000 | 12000 | 12000 |

attrs.desc: Number of skilled workers assigned to training in week t (they do not produce)
Number of skilled workers working 60h/week overtime in week t
Total worker-hours allocated to food I production in week t
Total worker-hours allocated to food II production in week t
Unmet demand for food I at end of week t (accumulates penalty)
Unmet demand for food II at end of week t (accumulates penalty)
Number of trained workers who have completed training and are working in week t

constraints.expr: d_hours_I[t] + d_hours_II[t] <= 40 * (50 - d_train[t] - d_overtime[t]) + 60 * d_overtime[t] + 40 * d_trained_active[t]  for all t

attrs.desc: Total production hours cannot exceed available worker-hours
Cannot train more skilled workers than available
Overtime only for non-training skilled workers

constraints.expr: d_trained_active[t] = sum of trainees who finished training by week t
d_hours_I[t] / 10 + d_backlog_I[t-1] - d_backlog_I[t] = demand_I[t]  for all t

attrs.desc: Food I supply meets demand or incurs backlog

constraints.expr: d_hours_II[t] / 6 + d_backlog_II[t-1] - d_backlog_II[t] = demand_II[t]  for all t

attrs.desc: Food II supply meets demand or incurs backlog
Must train 50 new workers by end of week 8
Each skilled worker can train up to 3 trainees in 2 weeks

constraints.expr: d_train, d_overtime, d_hours_I, d_hours_II, d_backlog_I, d_backlog_II, d_trained_active >= 0

relations.detail: Skilled workers in training do not produce
Each hour produces 10kg of food I
Each hour produces 6kg of food II
Overtime workers work 60h instead of 40h at 540 yuan/week

coupling_groups.implication: Hours allocated to food I and II compete for the same worker pool
Backlog accumulates week to week, increasing penalty
Training decisions now affect production capacity in future weeks
